title: MITM · pseudo-preimage

target.description: 10-round AES-256 compression pseudo-preimage with attacker-chosen IV and AES key/message. The figure has rounds0 through9, no final MixColumns, and terminal key addition.

setting.key_relation: The AES master-key input is chosen during public compression inversion; all round keys obey the standard schedule. No related secret keys or originally unknown master key are assumed.
setting.key_population: Attacker-controlled standard AES master-key input; no secret-key oracle
setting.plaintext_model: Jointly choose the 128-bit IV and complete standard AES message-key for one predetermined full128-bit output.
assumptions: Unit-cost access to a large sorted table; native time is reduced-primitive computations.
The standard AES key schedule is constrained; free key input is not independent arbitrary round keys.

time.note: Eqs4–7 include episode loops, key-path enumeration and matching; source-native reduced-primitive computation estimate.

data.note: Offline public compression problem; no secret oracle data collection.

memory.note: Source Table1/Figure path memory; not bytes, encryption counts or physical qubits. The main 2^48 footprint agrees with both blue/red lists; Section5.3 also prints 2^40 for the red key sublist although Figure8/Eq7 imply 2^48. No smaller full-memory bound is adopted.

preprocessing.note: Source key-path generation; included in the full algorithm time, not an additional independent budget.

success.description: The classical cost is an expected-solution MITM estimate; the source does not quantify a fixed-budget probability for the complete preimage event.

review.scope: PDF pp.20–22 Section5.3/Figure8/Eq15. Algorithm1 whole-output condition and expected episode count checked.

evidence.interpretation: Defining primary-text costs, output event and conditions checked together.

limitations: The complete named output probability is not quantified by the source.

experiment.distinctness: One pseudo-preimage pair (h,m); both IV and message-key are free under the standard AES key schedule.
experiment.reference: Ideal 128-bit compression output with a fixed target; generic classical work 2^128 and quantum search 2^64. DM and MMO notation correspond by swapping the two free inputs.
